transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, doc... mostly I'm here because I just don't sleep right anymore. I'll lay there for a long, long time, just staring up in the dark. And then when I finally do drift off, I wake up from bad dreams or... or just little noises, you know? 

Like Tuesday, I heard this rattling out back. Thought it was someone messing with my shed, but it was just a raccoon getting into the old tin cans. Big fat one, too. I used to hunt raccoons back when I was a boy. My uncle had these two hound dogs... beautiful animals, but loud as all get-out. You couldn't keep 'em quiet if a squirrel so much as sneezed in the next county. We'd stay out in the woods till near sunup sometimes. 

But, uh... what was I saying? Right, the noises. Once I wake up from a noise or a bad dream like that, I just can't seem to settle back down to sleep at all.
Do you find yourself feeling anxious or worried even when you're not trying to sleep, like during the day or while doing regular activities?

Yeah, I suppose I do. It ain't just the nights. Even during the day, when I go places now, I can't just walk in and relax. I always gotta look all around... check up high for what might fall on me, figure out exactly where the exits are. I even find myself testing the floor or the steps, making sure they're steady before I can sit easy. 

Like the other morning down at the diner. I was checking the floorboards by my table, and I noticed they got these new booths in there. Bright red vinyl. Reminds me exactly of the seats in my buddy Ray's old Chevy pickup. Lord, we drove that truck all the way down to Texas back in... must've been '71. Broke down twice on the way. Ray didn't know a wrench from a hole in the ground, so I had to fix the carburetor right there on the side of the highway. Hotter than a blister in the sun out there, I'll tell ya. We finally got it running with some baling wire and a prayer. He ended up selling that truck to a fella in town for two hundred bucks. 

But, uh... what was the question? Oh, right, being anxious. Yeah, I just gotta check a room top to bottom before I can settle down anywhere.
Do you ever find yourself bothered by thoughts or images that come into your mind uninvited and cause you a lot of worry or discomfort?

Well, yeah, I do. It ain't something I try to think about, but sometimes... if I hear a piece of metal scrape real loud, or even if I just see a ladder leaning up in somebody's yard, the whole thing just jumps right back in my head. It's like I'm right back under there again, just waiting and waiting for help to come. 

You know, speaking of ladders, my neighbor Jim leaves his out all year round. Just leaning right up against his gutters. I told him, "Jim, somebody's gonna steal that, or the wind's gonna knock it right through your window." But he's stubborn as a mule. He worked at the paper mill down by the river for near on forty years. Lost half his index finger in a press back in '82. Still grows the biggest tomatoes you ever saw, though. We used to slice 'em up thick, put a little salt and pepper on 'em... best eating in the world. My wife, God rest her soul, she used to make this homemade bread that was so soft... we'd sit out on the porch and eat tomato sandwiches till the sun went down and the lightning bugs came out. 

But, uh... I'm sorry, doc, my mind wanders. What were we talking about? Oh, the thoughts. Yeah, seeing a ladder or hearing that metal sound, it just puts me right back under there, clear as day.

When those thoughts or images come up, do you find yourself doing certain things over and over, like checking something again and again, or maybe thinking through a specific sequence in your head to try to make it better?

No, doc, I don't really do anything like that. I don't count or check things over and over or try to think a certain way to fix it. I just try to get away from it, I guess. 

You know, talking about doing things over and over, my brother-in-law Carl, he was a real stickler for routine. Every single morning, rain or shine, he'd walk down to the corner store and buy a newspaper and one of those little packs of powdered donuts. Never the chocolate ones, always the powdered. And he'd sit on the same green bench by the bus stop to eat 'em. The city tried to take that bench away back in '98 when they widened the road, but Carl actually went down to town hall and pitched such a fit they moved it back about three feet. He was a character, Carl was. He worked at the shoe factory for a while, but he got let go because he kept arguing with the foreman about how to lace the boots. Said there was only one right way to do it. 

But anyway... no, I don't have any routines or checking things like you're saying when those bad memories pop up. I just don't have anything like that.
Do you find yourself avoiding certain places or situations because you're worried about feeling anxious or having a hard time coping with it if you did?

Well, yeah, I guess I do stay away from some things now. Like, I keep finding reasons not to go down to the senior center these days. They always want me to come play Pinochle on Tuesdays. My buddy Earl, he's always calling me up about it. Earl's got this old basset hound named Buster. Ugliest dog you ever laid eyes on, I swear, ears dragging all over the floor. But smart, though. Earl taught him to fetch the morning paper, but Buster'd always stop and bury it in the neighbor's petunias if it was raining. The neighbor, Mrs. Higgins, she'd get so mad she'd come out waving her broom at that dog. She made the best peach cobbler, though. Used to bring it over in this heavy blue glass dish every Fourth of July. 

But, uh... where was I going with that? Oh, right, avoiding places. Yeah, I just make up excuses not to go to the center. And my own garage, too. I just don't want to go out there and work around it anymore... especially over near the tools and that spot where I used to keep that ladder. I just find a reason to stay inside instead.
Do you ever feel like you're reliving or right back in the middle of a scary or upsetting experience, almost like it's happening all over again?

Well, yeah, doc, that's kinda what I was getting at earlier when I brought up the sound of that metal scraping, or seeing a ladder in a yard. It ain't just a regular memory that pops up. It's... it's like I'm physically right back under there all over again. Trapped, you know? Just laying there waiting and praying for somebody to come help me. 

Speaking of waiting for help, the fella who finally did find me was the mailman, Mr. Abernathy. Now, Mr. Abernathy, he's been walking that same route for Lord knows how long. Got a real bad hitch in his step from when he fell off a horse back in his twenties. He used to breed quarter horses out near the county line, right next to where the old drive-in theater used to be. Beautiful animals, coats shiny as a new penny. My Uncle Pete had a horse once, named him Lightning because he was the slowest thing on four legs... just as a joke, you know? Uncle Pete was always making jokes like that. He used to wear these bright red suspenders every single day, even to church. Pastor didn't care for it much, but Pete didn't give a hoot. 

But, uh... I lost my train of thought again. I'm sorry. But yeah, to answer your question, it's just like I said before. I hear that scrape or see a ladder, and boom, I'm right back in the middle of it, just waiting under there.
